headline.suffix: what is truly happening in your application. Follow, analyze, and master all calls and interactions between the different components of your applications.

cta.title: Ready to transform your observability and a lot more?
cta.subtitle: Integrate INSPECT easily and get total visibility over your microservices in minutes.

profiles.title: Who can use INSPECT?
profiles.description: At first glance, one might think that INSPECT is only made for developers. But its added value lies in the fact that everyone can use it. Developers are, of course, the ones who need to implement it in the code. But after implementation, all profiles benefit from using it.

technical.title: Technical profile
technical.content: Technical profiles can check the health of microservices, if the deployment has errors. INSPECT can also be used for incident analysis, as a debugging tool to find the root cause. With the architecture view that updates automatically, you can easily spot the components that interest you, or detect potential antipatterns that might have gone unnoticed.

description.first: Quick diagnosis and root cause isolation
description.second: Monitoring the health of deployments and versions

functional.title: Functional profile
functional.content: A functional profile can easily identify a problem without asking the development team to check the logs, as INSPECT provides detailed information. It is also possible to see which queries are the most used, which helps prioritize the backlog. KPIs are accessible to better understand the query volume. INSPECT also allows generating an up-to-date architecture of your services to better understand the flows and interactions that occur over a given period.

description.second: Identification of queries and generation of KPIs
description.third: Up-to-date architecture to understand flows and interactions

redirect.profiles: More details on the use cases

description.description: A full package of tools in order to supervise, understand, and improve your application performances.

observability.title: Optimal observability
observability.content: Observing and diagnosing problems in complex systems has never been easier than after discovering INSPECT. You will get optimal observability across your applications

metrics.title: Master your metrics
metrics.content: Understand user trends, identify critical requests, and deliver the best user experience.

time.title: Detect incidents as quickly as possible
time.content: Monitor calls and application performance in real-time. Your end users will no longer encounter bugs or anomalies.

e2e.title: Track your end-to-end flows
e2e.content: Stop wasting considerable time searching logs across a multitude of services in vain. INSPECT allows you to track your end-to-end flows and directly determine which service interests you based on the event you want to analyze.

uniformize.title: Uniform traces
uniformize.content: INSPECT standardizes the types of traces collected. Everything is analyzed to ensure that anyone can understand the error information, even without specific technical knowledge.

heartbeat.title: Maximum monitoring
heartbeat.content: Monitor and supervise all the applications in your project. You will have access to the date of the last service restart, the deployed version, the number of attempts, and many other pieces of information, all within seconds.

features.title: INSPECT : a tool for telemetry, observability, and monitoring
features.subtitle: Total visibility for technical and functional teams, with zero code modifications.

observability.title: Observability
observability.subtitle: Understanding internal system state through external signals
observability.description: In a modern information system, a failure or slowdown can quickly impact customer experience and revenue. Observability allows you to see that an error has occurred, but more importantly, to understand why and how a process unfolded across the entire system. While traditional monitoring only raises isolated alerts, the INSPECT platform provides a unified, real-time view of application health, user journeys, APM, and component mapping. It brings together decision-makers, business leaders, and technical teams around a single source of truth.

value.title: What it brings to you:
value.desc: No more crisis meetings where teams blame each other. Observability enables everyone (business, support, developers) to understand within seconds what truly happened during an incident.

telemetry.title: Telemetry
telemetry.subtitle: Automatic and continuous collection of vital signals
telemetry.description: Telemetry refers to the automated collection of raw measurements and signals from the core of your applications: execution times, errors encountered, memory consumption, or the journey taken by a transaction. INSPECT provides objective, indisputable facts. You no longer rely on assumptions: every user action or nightly batch job has a timestamped factual record.

value.title: What it brings to you:
value.desc: Telemetry provides objective, indisputable facts. You no longer rely on assumptions: every user action or nightly batch job has a timestamped factual record.

dualTrace.title: Dual Event Trace
dualTrace.subtitle: Correlating two distinct traces (start and end) for every operation
dualTrace.description: INSPECT introduces the innovative Dual Event Trace method: emitting two distinct traces for a single operation. An initial launch trace signals that execution is underway, followed by a closing trace completing the full assessment (total duration, volume, success status, or errors). This approach enables real-time tracking of long-running processes, early bottleneck detection, and ensures that in the event of an abrupt crash, the interrupted operation remains clearly identifiable.
dualTrace.intro: INSPECT introduces the innovative Dual Event Trace method, which involves emitting two distinct traces for a single operation:

start.title: Launch trace (Start)
start.desc: Emitted immediately upon process initialization, it instantly signals to the server that the operation is running.

end.title: Closing trace (End)
end.desc: Emitted at the end of the operation, it complements the initial trace with the complete assessment (total duration, volume, success status, or details of exceptions).

value.title: Why is it a major added value for decision-makers and teams?

tracking.title: Real-time tracking of long-running processes
tracking.desc: No need to wait for a multi-hour job to complete to check if it has started properly or is currently in progress.

blockage.title: Early bottleneck detection
blockage.desc: If a process has started but does not emit its closing trace within normal timeframe, teams immediately spot the slowdown or blockage.

reliability.title: Enhanced operational reliability
reliability.desc: Even in the event of an abrupt server crash mid-processing, the start trace remains recorded, allowing you to know exactly which process was interrupted.

intro.subtitle: Continuous visibility into your application health
intro.description: Monitoring an application means keeping a constant watch on its state. INSPECT automatically detects every event (success or failure), execution speed metric, and anomaly, correlating business events with their technical traces.

traces.title: Execution traces
traces.description: The complete chronological journey of a request across the application, step by step.
traces.benefit: Know exactly where and why a transaction slowed down or failed.

metrics.title: Performance metrics
metrics.description: Periodic numerical indicators: average execution latency, request volume.
metrics.benefit: Assess overall application health and plan future capacity needs.

exceptions.title: Exceptions and errors
exceptions.description: Exceptions and errors are detected and logged with details to understand fully an anomaly
exceptions.benefit: Being able to make a diagnosis without technical skills, just by knowing how your application works functionnaly.

events.title: Events and execution contexts
events.subtitle: API, BATCH, Startup, Tests: understanding all forms of system activity
events.description: To monitor a set of applications, you need to monitor multiple methods and exchange protocols. They all transmit different information, in different ways and at different times: synchronous, asynchronous, at a regular frequency during the night, for a single occurrence by a user, etc.

unified.title: Unified Processing Visualization
unified.desc: Whether it is a click on a Web API, an overnight BATCH process, an application startup phase, or a test suite, INSPECT groups every activity into a structured execution Session.

context.title: Business and technical context
context.desc: Each session maintains its identity (duration, execution status, environment, application instance) for immediate diagnosis without unnecessary noise.

value.title: The INSPECT Advantage for Your Teams

first.title: Total visibility into batches
first.desc: Never discover too late that some task failed at 3 AM. INSPECT gives you full status, duration, and the exact failing item.

second.title: Instant API diagnostics
second.desc: Instantly pinpoint whether latency comes from your server, the network, or a third-party partner service.

third.title: Continuous quality validation
third.desc: Compare performance between releases during QA tests to prevent regressions from reaching production.

monitore.title: Monitoring external interactions
monitore.desc: An application rarely depends solely on itself. INSPECT automatically intercepts all outbound exchanges: database queries (JDBC), file transfers (FTP/SFTP), email sending (SMTP), directory queries (LDAP), or Web API calls (HTTP).

stages.title: Stages analysis (processing steps)
stages.desc: By breaking down each call into "stages" (steps), the solution precisely isolates the time spent in each subsystem to instantly identify the weak link.

user.title: User experience and journey analytics
user.description: Technical performance only matters if it delivers value to the end user. INSPECT links navigation journeys directly to the real performance felt by your customers.

concept.title: What is user journey and user experience (UX) in a web application?
concept.desc: Understanding the user's actions and overall experience when using the application.

journey.title: User journey
journey.desc: Refers to the sequence of steps, screens, and actions (clicks, inputs, navigations) a user takes to achieve a goal (e.g., logging in, searching for a file, submitting a form).

ux.title: User experience (UX)
ux.desc: Encompasses the user's overall perception: smoothness, display speed, clarity of flow, and absence of errors or technical blockages.

measurement.title: Measuring real user experience
measurement.desc: Using the lightweight Angular collector (@oneteme/inspect-ng-collector), INSPECT captures frontend activity directly in the user's browser.

universal.title: Bridging business and technical perspectives
universal.desc: Teams can track actual user navigation, identify friction or drop-off points, and determine whether perceived slowness is due to the network, the browser, or the server.

role.title: The role of INSPECT in navigation and user experience
role.subtitle: In many architectures, when a user encounters an anomaly or slowness, it is difficult to know exactly what they did.

router.title: State monitoring
router.desc: INSPECT detects each URL change and timestamps the transition times.

cache.title: Advanced behavior management
cache.desc: Takes into account the browser cache and page exits.

session.title: Session correlation
session.desc: Each view or navigation is linked to a logical session, propagating technical identifiers to backend HTTP requests.

dom.title: Automatic DOM (Document Object Model) event listening
dom.desc: A module in INSPECT automatically listens to DOM events, which are all basic user actions such as click, scroll, and load.

semantic.title: Intelligent resolution
semantic.desc: INSPECT identifies the targeted element without manual configuration by extracting its label through its technical attributes.

correlation.title: Immediate correlation with errors and performance

error.title: Direct attachment to anomalies
error.desc: Any crash or network slowdown is instantly linked to the exact action and the page where the user was.

analytics.title: The « Product Analytics (Beta) » module in INSPECT
analytics.subtitle: The Product Analytics module transforms technical traces into an exploitable visual timeline:

timeline.title: User journey timeline
timeline.desc: INSPECT provides an exact restitution of a session in the form of a chronological thread.

reproduction.title: Rapid incident reproduction
reproduction.desc: No need to ask the user to describe their steps, the scenario is easily reproduced.

insights.title: Understanding real usage
insights.desc: Product and development teams can identify the most used tabs and the less viewed screens.

intro.description: In modern architectures composed of multiple services, tracking the flow of information is often like looking for a needle in a haystack. INSPECT's End-to-End traceability automatically reconstructs the complete path of each transaction across all layers of the IT system.

pillars.title: Cartography and traceability are the tools that solve this problem

cartography.title: Cartography
cartography.desc: You can retrieve the real graph of interactions, even after modifications in your code that hasn't been updated in documentation yet.

traceability.title: End-to-End Traceability
traceability.desc: You can retrieve the exact sequence of an operation (steps, durations, executed requests...).

tree.title: Detailed Trace Tree
tree.description: A trace tree provides a complete hierarchical and chronological view of the path taken by a given business action (a user click, a transaction, or a batch).

diagnostic.title: Immediate Visual Diagnosis
diagnostic.desc: A manager or developer can determine at a glance the duration of a process. For example, a process that took 3 seconds does not have an equal duration across services. INSPECT allows you to know that the application code was processed in 50 ms but that the wait for an external database took 2950 ms, which is the majority of the request.

understanding.title: Interactive Temporal Graph
understanding.desc: INSPECT presents a visual tree where each solicited component appears as a chronological block.

thread.title: Multi-Thread
thread.desc: Multi-Thread is  de lancer plusieurs tâches simultanément dans un même programme. Chaque tâche est exécutée par un fil d'exécution (thread) distinct. INSPECT suit l'action utilisateur d'un thread à l'autre en propageant automatiquement le contexte de la session initiale à travers les différents threads d'exécution. Aucune rupture de traçabilité ne survient lors des opérations complexes en arrière-plan.

async.title: Asynchronism
async.desc: It's a task that can be executed in the background without blocking the main thread. It allows for better resource utilization and responsiveness. INSPECT provides a unified view of the main action and all related asynchronous tasks (parallel processing, notifications, database writes). If an asynchronous task fails, the user can trace back directly to the triggering event without losing any information, simplifying diagnosis and support.

cartography.title: Dynamic system cartography
cartography.description: As said before, INSPECT can automatically generate a living and real-time map of your information systems based on real flows.

map.title: Flow Map
map.desc: A graphical representation where each service, external partner, or database is visible, with visibility into real exchanges.

health.title: Real-time health status
health.desc: The cartography also allows checking the status of other internal services (more details in the "Lifecycle and Version Status" section).

urbanization.title: Mastering urbanization
urbanization.desc: Architects visualize real-time actual connections between applications, databases, and third-party services.

metrics.title: Performance Metrics and APM
metrics.description: Application Performance Monitoring (APM) transforms raw data into decision-making indicators (KPIs) to ensure compliance with service level agreements (SLAs) and anticipate infrastructure saturation.
metrics.chapters: INSPECT allows you to monitor key performance and reliability indicators of your applications, focusing on health, availability, performance, and volume.

control.title: Error Impact Analysis
control.desc: INSPECT allows centralized capture of exception stacks with intelligent depth limitation to target the root cause without overloading the display.

uptime.title: Continuous Availability Monitoring
uptime.desc: INSPECT also manages a measure of service uptime and automated calculation of error rates by application and environment.

latency.title: Latency / Waiting time
latency.desc: INSPECT allows you to identify latencies: the moments when the delay between the user clicking and the response being displayed on the screen occurs. Beyond averages that often hide the real problems, the display console (inspect-app) analyzes the distribution of response times over configurable windows (e.g., 30 min, 24 hours) to detect bottlenecks.

bottleneck.title: Bottleneck
bottleneck.desc: Detection of bottlenecks: the specific component (database, network, heavy computation) that slows down the entire chain. Identifying a bottleneck helps understand performance differences between various parts of your applications.

volume.title: Volume and Throughput
volume.description: Monitor the volume of transactions processed per second and anticipate load increases to ensure service smoothness.

rps.title: Throughput (RPS)
rps.desc: By tracking the number of requests, commands, or transactions successfully processed per unit of time, INSPECT allows you to better understand the throughput of your applications.

spike.title: Load Spike
spike.desc: Exceptional traffic moments are easily identifiable.

capacity.title: Capacity and Sizing
capacity.desc: Ability to anticipate load increases and size the infrastructure before server saturation.

resources.title: System and Machine Resources
resources.description: Here are the key indicators of your applications monitored by INSPECT

cpu.title: CPU
cpu.desc: A CPU saturated at 100% slows down all applications on the server. INSPECT monitoring its state ensures the reliability of your applications.

ram.title: RAM / JVM
ram.desc: INSPECT monitors the RAM (space where active data is stored). If it is full (Out of Memory), the application stops, so monitoring it is a primary need.

gc.title: Garbage Collector
gc.desc: The automatic mechanism that frees unused memory. If it takes too long to act, it causes noticeable pauses.

health.title: Lifecycle and version governance
health.description: You can have from INSPECT the possibility to track in real time the lifecycle of your applications, and to know which version is deployed on each server. INSPECT gives you the possibility to have a complete inventory of your applications, and to track all lifecycle events.

environments.title: Environments
environments.desc: You can have access to what is deployed on each environment (DEV, QA, PROD...) and on each application in a single web page.

versioning.title: Versions
versioning.desc: INSPECT provides all the information about the deployed application: version number, SHA of the last git commit, git tag. All the information needed to ensure what is deployed in which environment.

value.title: The INSPECT Advantage for Your Teams
value.subtitle: No more doubts about what is running on your servers

first.title: Instant visibility across the whole estate
first.desc: Find all deployed modules across the enterprise in a few clicks without bothering system administrators.

second.title: Detect version drift
second.desc: Immediately spot if a production server was missed during a security patch rollout.

third.title: Simplified audits and compliance
third.desc: Provide exact lists of running software during security reviews and governance audits.

events.title: Events history
events.description: Have a complete history of all lifecycle events, including deployments, restarts, and other operational changes.

deployments.title: Deployments
deployments.desc: INSPECT offers visibility into ongoing or completed deployments on your applications. You can easily see if there are any anomalies during staging or production deployments.

restarts.title: Reboot
restarts.desc: INSPECT can show you if a server restarted due to planned maintenance or an unexpected bug.

correlation.title: Easy analysis
correlation.desc: For example, if a service fails every day at a specific time, you can perform a preliminary analysis and understand that something at that time might be causing a bug.

intro.title: An autonomous system that self-optimizes, self-purges, and self-monitors
intro.description: Install a monitoring tool shouldn't give more tasks for the teams and should not be difficult to maintain. That's why INSPECT automatically manages its database, storage, and its own monitoring.

partitioning.title: Automatic data dartitioning
partitioning.description: To stay performant even with a large amount of data, INSPECT automatically organizes its data into partitions.

concept.title: Data Partitioning
concept.desc: An essential technique to keep searches ultra-fast over time.

partition.title: Partitions
partition.desc: Data partitioning helps INSPECT maintain fast searches, regardless of the application it is integrated into.

dynamic.title: Dynamic Automation
dynamic.desc: INSPECT automatically creates new partitions without any manual intervention.

retention.title: Smart retention and purge
retention.description: INSPECT optimizes storage by keeping short-lived technical traces for diagnostics and long-term functional business records for audits and compliance.

retention.title: Retention and retention differenciated
retention.desc: The policy determining how many days records are kept before automated cleanup.

purge.title: Smart Purge
purge.desc: INSPECT instantly and cleanly drops expired partition tables in milliseconds without CPU spikes.

value.title: The INSPECT Advantage for Your Teams
value.subtitle: Storage cost control and regulatory compliance

first.title: Substantial disk storage savings
first.desc: Prevent disk bloat by automatically pruning heavy, expired technical spans.

second.title: Regulatory compliance (GDPR & Audits)
second.desc: Meet data retention rules reliably without risking compliance oversights.

third.title: Simple centralized rules
third.desc: Define retention policies per module and let INSPECT enforce them automatically.

reporting.title: Self-Reporting
reporting.description: INSPECT agents continuously self-diagnose and protect host applications from any performance impact.

report.title: Self-Reporting
report.desc: The INSPECT agent's are able to measure its own resource usage and report transmission backpressure to make sure that the host application is not impacted.

circuit.title: Circuit-Breaker
circuit.desc: If INSPECT is saturated, it temporarily throttles collection to protect the host app's CPU and RAM.

installation.title: Installation
installation.content: Add INSPECT in your applications. Components to add for your front-end are inspect-app and inspect-ng-collector. For your back-end, it's inspect-core and inspect-server.

collector.title: inspect-ng-collector
collector.desc: Angular module for tracking HTTP requests and application lifecycle stages

core.title: inspect-core
core.desc: Java & Spring Boot dependency for thread tracking and system metrics capture

function.title: Function
function.jakarta: API used for the email management

architecture.title: Architecture
architecture.content: INSPECT is built around 3 pillars: Collectors (runtime telemetry libraries integrated into applications), Server (central ingestion, storage and lifecycle engine), and Application (web dashboard for monitoring and analytics).

application.title: Application
application.content: The inspect-app web dashboard transforms collected traces into intuitive charts, dynamic system dependency maps, and sequential timelines to inspect and diagnose applications.

collector.title: Collectors
collector.content: Lightweight libraries inspect-core (Java) and inspect-ng-collector (Angular) embed directly into your applications to record user actions, network calls, and errors without degrading application responsiveness.

server.title: Server
server.content: The central inspect-server ingests telemetry streams, cushions peak loads through in-memory buffering, partitions relational database tables for instant queries, and enforces retention policies.

flow.title: Flow
flow.content: Here is how information travels end-to-end between your applications and INSPECT components:

components.title: Technical components
components.content: INSPECT is composed of several technical components that work together to provide a comprehensive monitoring and analysis solution. These components include the collector, server, and application, as well as various libraries and tools that facilitate data collection, processing, and visualization.
